title: Filters and backdrop filters (support-aware)
learningObjectives: Explain filters and backdrop filters (support-aware) and use visual effects responsibly.

understand.concept: filter applies visual effects to an element's rendered content, while backdrop-filter applies effects to the area behind an element. Common functions include blur(), brightness(), contrast(), grayscale(), and drop-shadow(). backdrop-filter may need a translucent background to make the effect visible.
understand.whyItMatters: Filters can affect rendering cost and text clarity. backdrop-filter support and performance vary, so provide a readable fallback and test on target devices.
understand.analogy: A filter changes the view of an object; a backdrop filter changes the view through a translucent surface.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; CSS compositing and animation timelines follow browser rendering rules.

explain.narrative: The translucent panel blurs the backdrop where supported and retains a solid readable fallback otherwise.

examples.code: Readable content over a blurred backdrop
examples.explanation: The translucent panel blurs the backdrop where supported and retains a solid readable fallback otherwise.
examples.expectedOutput: A rendered example demonstrating the visual effect or animation behaviour.

practise.guidedTask: Create a card using filter:grayscale() and another using backdrop-filter:blur(). Add a fallback for unsupported backdrop filtering.
practise.independentTask: Build a visual component using the effect. Include a fallback, check contrast, and test keyboard and reduced-motion behaviour where relevant.
hints: Keep essential content independent of visual effects.
Check browser support and fallback behaviour.

questions.prompt: Which property applies a visual effect to the area behind an element?
questions.explanation: backdrop-filter applies graphical effects to the area behind an element.

questions.prompt: What should accompany an advanced visual effect?
options: A readable fallback and accessible content
Essential meaning available only through the effect
An assumption that all browsers support it
questions.answer: A readable fallback and accessible content
questions.explanation: Progressive enhancement keeps the interface usable when effects are unsupported or disabled.
